_comment: DISA Mozilla Firefox STIG-aligned enterprise policy for the IR Platform analyst
browser. policies.json is the STIG's prescribed enforcement mechanism (machine-wide,
not user-overridable). Controls below implement the STIG requirement set: no add-on
installation, no telemetry/data submission, no password manager or form autofill, no
sync/accounts, TLS 1.2 floor, pop-ups blocked, DoH disabled, developer tools off,
search suggestions off, and downloads always prompting. Kiosk scope is enforced too:
this browser exists to reach ONE origin — the SSO-gated platform frontend.

Certificates._comment: Trust the platform's own CA. ImportEnterpriseRoots also picks up the system store (populated by launch.sh from the mounted cert), so the SSO frontend loads without a TLS interstitial — analysts must never be trained to click through cert warnings.

WebsiteFilter._comment: Kiosk containment: allow ONLY the platform host — the SSO app (https) and the brokered Keycloak login (http), both of which terminate in the enclave via the broker. Everything else is blocked in-browser on top of having no network route. NOTE: Firefox match patterns must NOT include a port ('host:8443' is invalid and blocks everything), and the scheme IS matched — so both schemes are listed deliberately.

Preferences._comment_clipboard: Clipboard is an exfiltration vector out of a kiosk that displays forensic evidence: script-initiated copy/read would let a hostile page (or a curious user) lift case data off the contained browser. Deny page access to the clipboard in both directions; the analyst can still read on screen.
Preferences._comment_exfil: Downloads are permitted because evidence export is a supported analyst handoff, and every export is audited server-side. They are constrained rather than blocked: each download prompts (no silent writes), and files land in a fixed directory inside this ephemeral container, which has no internet route, no removable media and one brokered port to the platform. Moving a file off the kiosk is an operator action outside the browser's reach. Silent printing stays disabled — it is an unaudited path off the workstation.
